steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Still a little chilly, so early in the morning.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Typical of Shangshu's weather. Cool now, hot and hotter by noon. It's a fickle one.
There is rule to heat and cold. I presume Shangshu's folk have long since accustomed.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Indeed. But seeing the rain come harder lately, I'm worried the weather's about to turn.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Best it isn't some blistering cold or heat, so the people have a little time to adapt.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: The season is here. Shocking turns come as granted.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: Boatman, may you ferry me?

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: By all means. Where to?

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: Across the river.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Fine by me. How should this river of yours be crossed, in your view?

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Which route? Are you hurrying or taking your time?

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: What difference is there?

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: If you're in a rush, and time is short, I'll ferry fast. We'll reach the other shore without much effort.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: So what if I am not?

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Then we'll have to fix up some wine and sides before we cross.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: The wine's warmed aboard the boat, and we come from upstream to the crossing, staying to the side as we drift down. You can gaze on the city, and see the fields being planted. Fine scenery.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: Not half-bad.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Then so it'll be. I'll warm the wine now.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: You're deft at business.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: So this line of work goes. Always a need to play it by ear.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Few sirs like you would turn down viewing more of old Shangshu City. If it's not for the city, then it's for the people.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: Quite.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: The people deserve to be viewed. If not, then it's been a wasted journey.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: I imagine Liang Xun has informed you—he is to go with me this evening to return to the capital. The way out of Shangshu will be led by you.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: He did inform me.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Don't blame us. Mr. Liang's leaving in a rush here. Us folk can't help but be worried.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Our Magistrate... As good as a parent to us, we say, but he's still young in the end. Resembles the nephews of our own at times. There's concern to be had.

steps.name: Grand Tutor
steps.text: Liang Xun has the talent, and the resolve. Should he withstand, he will be famed and recognized.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: And what if he doesn't?

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: —*sigh* No, never mind, I shouldn't ask. If you want to see Shangshu, just come with me.

steps.name: Boatman
steps.text: Only shame is, young Lee's still searching for someone right now. He'll be hard-pressed to meet Mr. Liang this evening if he wants, I think.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: 'Tis still quite cool. 'Tis lucky we are not cold ourselves, with the tea warm.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Official affairs inundate you, my Lord. What brings you here so early?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I agreed to watch the play with you.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Cloak in some more layers. Mind the chill.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: When did we agree this? All I had said was to come if you were free.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: And I'm free today.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Liar. Your work is surely a mountain of bother, with the Grand Tutor so urgent in handing it over to you... Could it be, my Lord, you did not sleep last night?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: *cough* I did get a little shuteye.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: You're also early to rise today, Miss Ning.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: I guessed the headstrong Liang would come at first light despite all exhortation, and so was awaiting you the whole time.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: That. Hm. I...

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Your tea cup is empty. Pass it to me.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: 'Tis but a cup of tea. Need we such formalities between us?

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: 'Tis pleasant, to be able to sit here in this mountain, drinking tea, shaking oneself awake.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: The refreshments at this shop are quite fine too... the shaobing, sesame cake, and—

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Sweet fritters.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: You've lauded this place before.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Ah, and you remembered?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Mm. Being that you're fond, I take note.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Everything of Shangshu is fine, save the slight strength in flavor. Lucky that the pastries by and large are tender and sweet still. They fit my palate.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: *sigh* Your estate stews were very spicy at first, my Lord. Though, they have been considerably better since.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: I could not pick up my chopsticks before needing to seek water. How very sorry for me.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: The estate has spice-remedying decoction available at all times.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Miss Ning, your home...

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: The waterways of the south. We are no great spice eaters.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I apologize for the trouble.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: What matter is it? We all must adapt at some point.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: So you say, though it's not so easily done.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: 'Tis not hard, should you intend to.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: We all must adapt at some point.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Verily.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: You have mentioned you are native to Shangshu, my Lord?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I am.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I left home at an early age, and only returned in recent years. You know as much, Miss Ning.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: I have heard you make mention.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Is it then that you met your Lungmen friend, in your period away?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I knew nothing back then, left to forge my own way, made no shortage of friends, believed the spirit of youth could conquer everything, accomplish anything...

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I did plenty of clownishly ridiculous, foolish things.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: 'Tis no foolish thing to make friends.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: My Lord, the friend you have made is a fine one.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: ...I was simply lucky to.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Were it not for such urgent affairs, 'twould only be right we bid your friend on a true, proper tour of Shangshu, being the hosts that we should.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: 'Twould also be more chance to hear some anecdotes of your past, my Lord. Who knows how different you are these days?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I have never changed.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Maybe I have changed some. But...

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: What I set out to do, for these common peoples... has never changed.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: When the Grand Tutor last evening proposed I accompany him to the capital... I didn't want to accept, at first.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: You denounce me for accepting in your place?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: No. I hardly could.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I should not have hesitated in the first place. I should be thanking you, Miss Ning.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: So long as you do not blame me. I understand you are uneasy for Shangshu, as can others, but the Grand Tutor's word is a different story.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: He keeps no mediocrity for company. What he assigns are but the most rugged, hard-fought opportunities.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: I believe, should my perception of you not be faulty, that if you had refused in a moment of hesitation, you would surely regret it in time.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I understand... I apologize for worrying you.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: ...Heheh.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Miss Ning...?

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Ah, no, nothing. I just suddenly imagined...

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: If you had then and there earnestly, unreservedly agreed to leave, I fear I would perhaps have been quite angry.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Ahem. You're joking, Miss Ning.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: I am certainly not joking.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: *cough* *cough* *cough*.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: In so little time, the sun has come up.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: My Lord, are you enjoying this play?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: It's not bad.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Then shall you be descending the mountain sooner?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I'll watch another while.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Miss Ning, watch another while.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Okay, come on, Dad! Stop looking at it!

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Why? What's even the point? It's just a travel itinerary! Me and the guys already hashed it out! We're leaving once everything's packed!

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: And I have a whole ROOM of stuff that still needs packing, so!

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: What's the rush? Let me look over it again...

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: You're a group of young people. You rush your decisions. That's a recipe for disaster.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: What's wrong with young people? You were all young once, right? Didn't you go all over when you were young, Dad?

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: Is that a fair comparison?

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: Without anyone to accompany you, will you be sure of which ways you can go, and which you can't?

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: For this long a journey in this season, do you even know what you should bring, and what you shouldn't?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Dad!

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Times have changed! Stop lecturing me about your old days!

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: Yaoye! Listen, there's not much your dad can tell you, so...

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: If you're sure you're going to Yumen, then go. I couldn't stop you all anyway. Avoiding the path we laid out for you might just be for the better...

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Dad, suppose, um, and I'm just picturing...

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Suppose we don't run our inn here, you've still got a couple cousins. Have you considered going with us to Yumen?

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: Yaoye, ah...

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Ugh, dad, I'm just wondering out loud, I know it's not gonna happen! You can just listen or something...

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: Yaoye.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: ...*sigh*.

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: This inn was meant to be left to you. If you're not taking it, we may as well close up shop sooner rather than later.

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: If you want to set up your own business, I won't stop you. I trust you to have thought it through. But I still need to tell you a thing or two, and I don't want you to think I'm prattling.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Dad...

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: You're leading all those youths. They trust you, follow you. You say times have changed... You're right, times have changed, but this sort of thing doesn't change no matter what the times are.

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: You step forward, and they're there all at once, so no matter how difficult it gets in future, you can't back down. No matter how tough, how exhausting, you have to bear it. Do you hear me?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: I... I know, Dad.

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: ...*sigh*. Alright, take the itinerary. I've kept you off of some of the tougher roads. If you can stick to the highways, do so. Never revisit those same muddy paths we waded through.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: No need to worry.

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: It's hard, not worrying.

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: I have a worry, right this moment.

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Go on.

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: Yaoye, you're not young anymore. When you go to Yumen, can you possibly try and bring back a decent young man...?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Stop, stop!

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Dad! That is SO stupid to worry about!!

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: How is it stupid?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: It just is!

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: Ugh, jeez, I'm not talking to you anymore. I need to go to Mr. Liang's place anyway.

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: What do you want Mr. Liang for?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: I'm not the one looking for him, it's that stupid Lee guy!

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: If Lee can't find him, Mr. Liang's not likely to be at the estate. What use would you have for going?

steps.name: Miss Du
steps.text: That makes sense. Yeah, okay! He's just using the same trick again to dupe me! I'm gonna go find him and GET MINE!

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Innkeeper Zheng
steps.text: You proud little girl. When will you finally settle down...?

steps.name: Leizi
steps.text: Do not pry into others' domestics.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Your concern is unnecessary.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Lin Qingyan, what do you mean by this?

steps.name: Leizi
steps.text: Eat your food.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: You know I'm not referring to that.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: You were waiting here from sun-up, so you could hold me from visiting those three. You have to have some reason for me.

steps.name: Leizi
steps.text: I told you, I'll go with you.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Lin Qingyan!

steps.name: Leizi
steps.text: You're making a scene. Look at yourself.

steps.name: Leizi
steps.text: I did not make this trip in my capacity with the Central Judicial Office. Disregarding our positions, what should you be calling me?

steps.name: Leizi
steps.text: Are you forgetting the rule?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: ...Auntie.

steps.name: Leizi
steps.text: Good.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Why do you always bring this out to stifle me? It's not as if you're an honest relative. You're just relying on the friendship between the Lins and my dad, and being a generation older.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Just why did the Tianshi Bureaus have you make this trip?

steps.name: Leizi
steps.text: For the common people, naturally.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: How nice for the common people.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: If that's the case, will you really just ignore... will you really just carry on like this?

steps.name: Leizi
steps.text: The Grand Tutor has made his judgment. I may simply await orders.

steps.name: Leizi
steps.text: But you, Zuo Le.

steps.name: Leizi
steps.text: Within the Sui Regulator, you're still green. What is concealed behind this trip to Shangshu is not simple, and as it seems now, you have no awareness of the inside details.

steps.name: Leizi
steps.text: Dispatched yet barely cognizant. Ridiculous! Who called you here?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: No one sent me. I volunteered myself.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: What? Don't you believe me?

steps.name: Leizi
steps.text: I do.

steps.name: Leizi
steps.text: I believe you volunteered yourself, but I also believe there are strange actors behind this.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: This is my first time hearing that the impartial, incorruptible, honest, forthright Lin Qingyan of the Central Judicial Office has learned to speculate on the bureaucracy's murky secrets.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Don't rumors say you're sick of giving those sorts of shameless busybodies the time of day? That if anyone tries to wag on at you, you shock their brain numb?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: This, right now, is far from your style.

steps.name: Leizi
steps.text: You have no need to point fingers at my style of affairs.

steps.name: Leizi
steps.text: I'm entrusted with your care. When things concern you, it's only natural I exercise some caution.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: ...Tch.

steps.name: Leizi
steps.text: Did you click your tongue at me?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I did not. You misheard, Auntie.

steps.name: Leizi
steps.text: Once this matter is through, you should return with me to the capital as well.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Leizi
steps.text: General Zuo desires it.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Understood. I will accompany you back.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Assistant Minister of Rites... 'tis not a post that participates too much in government affairs.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Did you ever hear, my Lord, how this position of mine came to be?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I'd like to.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: You rose upon your own excellence; this I cannot compare to.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: The Ning family... 'tis major in a sense. Sordid that its ancestors were, its descendants did progress. Generations accumulated propriety, connections and assets, and so things passed down.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: My father's father was an official, first rank, assiduous for quite some decades. You should know him even if I did not tell you his name.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: I would only be ready to say so to you, my Lord, lest it seem I was flaunting.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Hardly.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Miss Ning... you are a fine one.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: I knew you would not think so.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: I have told you, too, that I rank seventh within my own generation.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Good.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: My father's generation sought otherwise, as did the one below. My oldest cousin is on my father's side, ten or so years my senior, and has long settled himself down.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: As my grandfather prepared to retire from officialdom, so I was at junior vigor's peak, and became drawn into a smuggling and embezzlement case. By a fluke I caught a string of thieves, and the documents landed on my grandfather's desk the following day.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Your ability excels, Miss Ning.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Pleasantry.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: I would never. It is my honesty.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Then I will believe you.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: My grandfather called me to his study alone; we conversed of little in particular, before he asked me this one question.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: He asked: 'Ciqiu, would you be willing to give your ability and learning for the country, the people, and for the realm?'

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: And I replied...

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: ...You would offer your life.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Without hesitance.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Your spirit is bold, Miss Ning.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Enough, now. The story ends here.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: My Lord, your tea is cold.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: It's still somewhat warm.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: But I notice your hands are cold now, my Lord. If you would be willing to have half this cloak back from me, 'tis not out of the question we could steep a freshly brewed pot.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Health is crucial. Wear it well. Don't take it off.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: I am fine. If you do not believe, shall we test... if I am warmer than you?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: My hands are cold. Don't be chilled, Miss Ning.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Aiya!

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: After today, I don't know when we'll find the chance to meet again.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Take more care of your health, Miss Ning. Don't let the cold tempt you.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Should...

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Should you ever wish to view the flowers in future, and don't deem it too far-flung, then you needn't take it upon yourself. Have someone take a letter, and send them to me to plant.

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: Miss Ning?

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Right, ah, um...

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: Well... Given you speak so, I will be straightforward too.

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: My Lord, how much longer are you going to keep that ribboned jewelry case in your pocket?

steps.name: Liang Xun
steps.text: ...Ahem. This is...

steps.name: Miss Ning
steps.text: What, my Lord? Could you have possibly intended to give that to another?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Ugh, can't stand it.

steps.name: Pole-Carrier
steps.text: We shouldn't have taken you to him.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Shouldn't have.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Won't you show yourself?

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Wouldn't work, showing myself now.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Their whole back-and-forth's more of a work of art than any stage play.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Who knew old Liang would... *sigh* Never we mind.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: No... That won't do. I do mind!

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Who knew after a decade and change apart, Liang would turn out like this!

steps.name: Pole-Carrier
steps.text: A decade and change apart. It's not uncommon.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: It gets to me.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: At least there's still tea to drink, and a play to watch.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: Well, Liang Xun, you owe me another now.

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Lee
steps.text: One last cup of wine with an old friend really is difficult to swing.
